pages.lesson:
LESSON: READING 2.4.1 INTENSIVE READING: CLASS READER

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: Why should we not judge a book by its cover?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book
2. describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book
   In simple words: practise until you can explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

2. describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place
   In simple words: practise until you can describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place. Use examples from school and home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: Talk about Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader using something you see at school in Kenya.

Example 2: Give a home example from your county, estate, or village.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Underline two new ideas about Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader in the examples.
2. Explain Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader to a parent using one local example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader.
4. Show that you can: explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader using examples from school or home.
2. Answer: Why is Reading 2.4.1 Intensive Reading: Class Reader important for a Grade 7 learner?
3. Make a one-minute oral presentation to a parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Study the cover page of a class reader, read the blurb and highlight the outstanding features,
2. Discuss the title of the class reader,
3. Learning to Learn: It is enhanced as learners build on their learning experiences through analysis of the setting and research on the author.
4. Critical thinking is developed as learners explore the links between different events through tasks like creating graphic organisers that cultivate high-order thinking skills.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. explain the different parts that aid in previewing a book
2. describe the author and the setting of the text in terms of time and place

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
